body_markdown:
A self-storage unit in New York City is incredibly useful because it creates space for the clothing, furniture, décor, and sporting equipment that do not fit into your apartment. **Use self-storage as a second closet, organize seasonal belongings, and clear living space without parting with items you plan to use again.**


New York City apartments often require a thoughtful approach to storage. When closets, bedrooms, entryways, and living areas fill up, a nearby storage unit gives you a place to pack away items that are out of season or not part of your daily routine.


## **The Basics**


- Use self-storage to clear space in a New York City apartment where space is at a premium and hard to come by.
- Store seasonal items, furniture, décor, sporting equipment, and other items you do not use every day.
- Use a storage unit as a backup closet for seasonal clothing since most NYC apartments don’t have closet space to spare.
- Choose a unit near your home, workplace, or along a regular transit route. If storing specialty sporting equipment, choose a location along the route to your destination.
- Use the[Public Storage Size Guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) to find the size unit you need and enjoy their month-to-month rental agreements to match storage to your needs, even if they’re seasonal.


### **Use Self-Storage to Create More Space in Your NYC Apartment**


**Self-storage creates space and reduces clutter in your NYC apartment by moving less-used belongings out of closets, bedrooms, and living areas.** Instead of letting overflow fill a spare corner or crowd an entryway, pack away items that do not fit into your current routine.


Use a storage unit for:


- Seasonal clothing/shoes and décor
- Extra furniture
- Sporting equipment
- Suitcases and travel gear
- Small appliances and kitchen supplies
- Home décor you plan to rotate back into your apartment


Self-storage helps you restore room for the activities and belongings you use every day. And less clutter in your living space will allow you to clear your headspace clearer also.


### **Use a Storage Unit as a Second Closet**


**A storage unit works as a second closet by giving you room to rotate seasonal clothing, bedding, shoes, and accessories.** Pack away heavy winter coats, boots, sweaters, and cold-weather bedding during New York’s warmer months, then switch them out when the seasons change.


Keep your clothing organized with a simple system:


- Wash and dry clothing fully before packing it away for storage.
- Group items by season and category in clearly labeled bins or garment bags.
- Place the next season’s items near the front of the unit for easy access.
- Keep an inventory list in your phone or notebook.


This rotation helps you keep your apartment closet focused on the clothes you wear now. Cleaning clothing before storing also keeps it in better condition and reduces chances of degradation over time.


### **Choose a Location That Fits Your Routine**


**Choosing a storage location that fits your routine makes seasonal swaps, drop-offs, and pickups easier.** Find one of the 60 New York City-area Public Storage locations near your apartment, workplace, or a regular transit route that works best for you.


If you store specialty sporting equipment, choose a storage location that fits your route to the activity. For example, a skier living in NYC heading out to the Catskills to Hunter Mountain or Windham Mountain might choose storage on the way out of the city like the facility at 1137 Route 300 in Newburgh, NY for ski storage. Similarly, a Manhattan-dwelling golfer who often plays Van Cortlandt Park Golf Course might choose to store their golf equipment at the nearby Public Storage facility at 385 Gerard Avenue in the Bronx.


Search the map of all 60[Public Storage locations in New York City](https://www.publicstorage.com/self-storage-ny-new-york) to compare unit sizes, locations, and available features like 24/7 Access (available at 31 facilities), Drive-Up Access (available at 44 facilities), and Climate-Controlled storage (available at 55 of the 60 area facilities).


### **Choose the Right Self-Storage Unit Size**


**Choosing the right self-storage unit size in New York City for your apartment overflow depends on what and how much you plan to store.** Start by measuring furniture or hanging clothing racks, then count how many boxes and other items will be stored and then deciding how often you expect to access your items. A smaller unit often works for seasonal clothing and boxes, while larger units fit furniture and belongings from more than one area of your apartment.


**Unit Size & Storage Need** **Typical Fit**


**5′ x 5′** Seasonal clothing, shoes, décor, sports gear, and boxes


**5′ x 10′** Contents from one room, including boxes, small furniture, and seasonal items


**10′ x 10′** Furniture, boxes, and belongings from several rooms


**10′ x 15′ or Larger** Furniture and household items from a larger apartment or multi-room project


Include extra space if you plan to visit often and want to include room for an aisle to access items throughout the year. Use the[Public Storage Size Guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) before reserving, which can be done easily online in minutes without a credit card.


### **Organize Your Unit for Quick, Easy Access**


**Organizing your self-storage unit for easy access helps you find the items you need quickly without unpacking the entire space.** As the songs say, things move quickly in NYC, so every second matters! Label every bin with its contents, room, and season, then group similar belongings together.


Follow these general storage tips:


- Pack clean, dry items only. This will make retrieval nicer.
- Place heavier bins and furniture on the floor and stack lighter bins on top or on shelving.
- Put frequently used or accessed items near the entrance.
- Leave a clear aisle from the door to the back wall if you’ll need access to all items while storing.
- Store bins by category, such as “Winter Clothing,” “Holiday Décor,” or “Sports Equipment.”
- Update your inventory after every seasonal swap.


Do not store food, perishables, wet items, live plants, hazardous materials, or sensitive documents in a self-storage unit.


### **Keep Storage Flexible with a Month-to-Month Rental**


**Month-to-month self-storage keeps your rental flexible when your NYC storage needs change in a New York minute or with the season, a move, a renovation, or an apartment transition.** Public Storage rentals are all month-to-month, so you can rent storage for the time you need without signing a long-term agreement. Use a storage unit for one season, during a move, or as part of a longer-term organization plan. Public Storage also allows customers to complete a storage rental online in minutes in case an apartment you find during your wild NYC apartment rental search isn’t available at the perfect time and you need to store your belongings for a few days in between moves.


### Frequently Asked Questions


**How Can I Create More Space in My NYC Apartment?**


You can create more space in your NYC apartment by moving seasonal clothing, furniture, décor, sporting equipment, and other less-used items into one of the 60 self-storage units in the New York City area. This approach clears closets, walkways, bedrooms, and living areas for the belongings you use every day.


**Can I Use a Storage Unit as a Second Closet?**


You can use a storage unit as a second closet by rotating seasonal clothing, shoes, bedding, and accessories throughout the year. Pack items in labeled bins or garment bags, keep the next season’s items near the entrance, and choose one of the 60 convenient locations in the New York City metro area along your commute or close to your apartment for easy access.


**What Size Self-Storage Unit Do I Need in NYC?**


The size storage unit you need in New York City depends on the items you will store, but you can begin by measuring larger furniture, counting boxes, and deciding how often you plan to visit the unit. A 5′ x 5′ unit fits seasonal items and boxes, while a 5′ x 10′ or larger unit fits furniture and belongings from one or more rooms. Use the[Public Storage Size Guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) to find the perfect unit size for your needs, whether it’s a second closet, holiday décor storage, or ski storage in New York City.


**Where Should I Choose a Storage Unit in New York City?**


You should choose a unit at one of the 60 conveniently located Public Storage facilities in New York City near your home, workplace, or regular transit route. If you store specialty sporting equipment, choose a location along the route to your activity or destination.


**Can I Rent a Public Storage Unit for Only One Season?**


You can rent a Public Storage unit in New York City, or in any of the 4,600 locations across 42 states in the US, for only one season or as long as you need to store your items thanks to Public Storage’s month-to-month rental agreements. This flexibility supports seasonal clothing swaps, temporary moves, apartment transitions, and ongoing organization needs.
